Alkaline phosphatase deficiency causes defining skeletal hypomineralization and rickets; renal injury and seizures are not established in >=30%.
Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; renal salt loss reflects aldosterone deficiency rather than intrinsic renal damage.
MELAS is a mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like brain injury; other organ frequencies are unestablished for this subtype.
Intellectual disability, primary hypogonadism and ichthyosis define the syndrome; strabismus affects 80-99%.
Muscular dystrophy is a primary degenerative skeletal muscle disorder; no evidence establishes additional organ involvement.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure (8/10) and dysphagia (10/10) reflect respiratory and bulbar muscle dysfunction, without established lung or GI injury.
Basal cell carcinoma originates in skin.
Thymic epithelial tumour: thymus has no listed axis. It is not lymphoma or a blood-cell neoplasm; associated autoimmune diseases are separate.
Thiamine deficiency with defining cardiac dysfunction and high-output heart failure; neuropathy is not obligatory in the wet form.
Neoplasm originating in the brainstem.
Hereditary heterotaxy with congenital cardiovascular malformations; organ malposition alone is not damage, and asplenia frequency is unestablished.
THRA resistance commonly causes skeletal maturation defects, neurodevelopmental impairment and anemia, each >30%; constipation alone does not establish GI damage.
Congenital obstruction of the hymen is a reproductive tract disorder outside the listed axes.
Inherited retinal degeneration with hemorrhage, exudation and progressive visual loss; pseudoinflammatory does not establish immune mediation.
Inherited retinal and choroidal degeneration causing visual field loss.
Intellectual disability, skeletal dysplasia/patellar instability and hypogonadism define the syndrome; premature balding occurs in 80-99%.
Malignant lymphoid-cell tumour arising within the eye; lymphoma warrants hematologic and immune mechanism axes. Later CNS disease is not automatically included.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation confined predominantly to bone marrow; no defining skin disease or common additional organ damage.
Mitochondrial Leigh syndrome; cardiomyopathy and liver dysfunction each occur in 30-79%. Frequent skeletal myopathy omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Splenic hyperfunction causes excessive blood-cell destruction; spleen as a blood organ belongs to the hematologic axis.
Isolated dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; laryngeal and limb contractions do not establish intrinsic airway or skeletal muscle disease.
Neurodevelopmental, cardiac and skeletal defects define the syndrome; hydronephrosis/reflux occur in 30-79%. Frequent dental malocclusion omitted at the cap.
RP1-related retinal photoreceptor degeneration with night blindness, visual field constriction and reduced acuity.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the lung; mucinous morphology does not imply gastrointestinal origin or involvement.
